def public_meta(self, is_head: bool = False) -> dict:
        """Version metadata safe to expose to any capability-URL holder."""
        git = self.source.get("git") if self.source_type.startswith("git") else None
        return {
            "version": self.version,
            "title": self.title,
            "status": self.status,
            "note": self.note,
            "created_at": self.created_at,
            "is_head": bool(is_head),
            "size_bytes": len(self.html.encode("utf-8")),
            "source_type": self.source_type,
            "author": {
                "project_id": self.author.get("project_id"),
                "project_name": self.author.get("project_name"),
                "stack_host": _stack_host(str(self.author.get("stack_url") or "")),
            },
            "git": git,
        }
claim: Public metadata returns the submitted Git repository URL for Git-sourced versions without any reader password or caller authorization, exposing private repository location metadata (and potentially embedded URL userinfo) to anyone holding the artifact capability URL.
trigger: A user publishes an artifact with a private repository URL and an unguessable artifact URL is disclosed; an unauthenticated caller requests GET /a/{id}/meta (or a caller only supplying the artifact password). read_meta merges head.public_meta(), which copies source.git including the original URL into the JSON response. _validate_git_url accepts HTTPS URLs with userinfo, so embedded credentials are not excluded before storage.
impact: A capability-URL holder can learn the private repository host/organization/name and, if userinfo was supplied in the URL, receive that credential material, defeating the documented expectation that public metadata contains no sensitive owner/source details and enabling cross-tenant disclosure even when artifact content is protected.

evidence.detail: src/main.py:1515-1537 read_meta is a public route and directly merges head.public_meta(is_head=True); it explicitly says metadata is available even when password-protected.
src/main.py:954-961 stores the submitted git_url in source['git']['url'] while intentionally omitting only clone credentials.
src/builder.py:541-551 _validate_git_url checks only scheme and hostname and does not reject URL userinfo.
tests/test_api.py:417-430 verifies public metadata shape but does not assert that git source URLs are redacted or withheld.

expected_behavior_source: src/main.py:1519 describes this as public metadata with no owner details and src/store.py:303-306 says public_meta is safe for any capability-URL holder; private repository location and any embedded credential material are source metadata that should not be exposed absent explicit authorization.
suggested_fix: Reject URL userinfo and do not include the raw git source URL in public_meta/read_meta; expose only a redacted host or an owner/author-authorized field, with regression tests for private Git metadata.
